title: Extract duplicated email regex into a shared validators module
description: Migration task on refactor_extract_function: the same email regex is duplicated in cli.py, handlers.py, and models.py. Extract it into src/validators.py as is_valid_email(email) and update all three files to import from there.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate the duplicated email validation logic into a shared module.

1. Create src/validators.py with:
   import re
   EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r'^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$')
   def is_valid_email(email: str) -> bool:
       return bool(EMAIL_RE.match(email))

2. Update src/cli.py: remove the inline regex; import and call is_valid_email from src.validators.

3. Update src/handlers.py: remove the inline regex; import and call is_valid_email from src.validators.

4. Update src/models.py: remove the inline regex; import and use is_valid_email from src.validators.

All 6 existing tests in tests/test_validation.py must still pass.
Also add tests/test_validators.py testing is_valid_email directly.
required_artifacts: cli.py imports is_valid_email from src.validators; no inline regex
handlers.py imports is_valid_email from src.validators; no inline regex
models.py imports is_valid_email from src.validators; no inline regex
success_criteria: uv run pytest tests/ -v passes (all tests)
uv run python -c "from src.handlers import handle_signup" passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?

check_commands.build: uv run python -c "from src.handlers import handle_signup"
